brief: Goldman Sachs keeps a neutral 3-month cross-asset stance and a modestly pro-risk 12-month one: OW equities, N bonds, commodities and cash, UW credit. The chain runs: higher nominal growth drove a procyclical rotation over the summer, so equities outperformed bonds even as long-dated yields neared post-GFC highs on cyclical support, AI debt issuance and fiscal concerns. That prompted US Treasury intervention in long-dated Treasuries, which weighed on the Dollar and boosted Gold. Because bonds now act as a speed limit for equities and buffer less, GS pushes style diversification (low volatility, high dividend yield), Gold and real assets, and a barbell against AI concentration. Sustained double-digit earnings growth should keep equities ahead of bonds and credit over 12m, but peaked revisions imply slower returns and lower Sharpe ratios. Economists forecast 2.1% US Q4/Q4 GDP growth, 2.9% core PCE in December and the Fed on hold at 3.5-3.75%, with a September BOJ hike and further ECB hikes more likely. Near-term risks are rates volatility, seasonal weakness, US midterms and geopolitics. After August's implied-vol reset GS prefers option spreads against a correction rather than a bear market.
